# dtrtrs

> Solves a triangular system of the form A·X = B or Aᵀ·X = B.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dtrtrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtrtrs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dtrtrs( order, uplo, trans, diag, N, nrhs, A, LDA, B, LDB ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | `'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'`<br>One of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'`. |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | `'unit'` or `'non-unit'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand side columns<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$  (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose = Transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `A`: The triangular matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of the array A contains the upper triangular matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of the array A contains the lower triangular matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are also not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dtrtrs.ndarray(
    uplo, trans, diag,
    N, nrhs,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB
) → integer
```

Solves a triangular system of the form `A * X = B`, `A**T * X = B`, or `A**H * X = B` where `A` is a triangular matrix of order `N` and `B` is an `N`-by-`NRHS` matrix.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether `A` is upper or lower triangular |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | Specifies the operation to be performed<br>One of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'`. |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | Specifies whether `A` is unit or non-unit triangular |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand side columns<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Right-hand side matrix, overwritten with solution |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$  (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose = Transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `A`: The triangular matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of the array A contains the upper triangular matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of the array A contains the lower triangular matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are also not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the i-th diagonal element of A is zero, indicating that the matrix is singular and the solutions X have not been computed.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dtrtrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtrtrs';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const B = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dtrtrs( 'row-major', 'upper', 'no-transpose', 'non-unit', N, N, A, N, B, N );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dtrtrs.ndarray( 'upper', 'no-transpose', 'non-unit', N, N, A, N, 1, 0, B, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DTRTRS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DTRTRS solves a triangular system of the form

$$
A \, X = B \quad\text{or}\quad A^T \, X = B
$$

where A is a triangular matrix of order N, and B is an N-by-`NRHS` matrix. A check is made to verify that A is nonsingular.

</section>
